Per-36 is a production rate, not an assumption that everyone plays 36 minutes. Projected minutes include a small training-based overtime allowance. Out players and players outside the estimated rotation are excluded. Historical tests exclude players' first three recorded appearances; rookie projections are marked uncertain.

Only forecasts saved before tip-off count. Historical validation is kept separate. Missing appearances are not graded as zero or a loss. No sportsbook line or betting return is implied.

PER-36 FOUNDATION, VALIDATED CONTEXT

Historical stat counts are divided by minutes and scaled to 36, with recency weighting and shrinkage for limited samples. A separate minutes model estimates playing time. A context model refines per-36 rates using prior role, rest, pace and opponent scoring context. All pregame features exclude the game being predicted.

We compared rolling per-game averages, shrunk per-36 × projected minutes, and learned per-36 rates × projected minutes. The context model won the validation comparison. Training uses 2017–22 seasons, validation uses 2022–25, and the final reported test is 2025–26.

FINAL HISTORICAL TEST · 2025–26

26,261 recorded player appearances with at least three earlier appearances. The final test was evaluated after model selection; no fit or selection uses its outcomes. Current-roster injury/minutes allocation is not replayed in these tests.

StatMean absolute errorP10–P90 observed coverageNegative log score

A nominal P10–P90 range targets 80% coverage. The observed coverage above is the actual historical result; points and PRA ranges can be too narrow. Over/under percentages should be treated as provisional. Lower MAE and log score are better.

UNCERTAINTY & AVAILABILITY

  • Overdispersed negative-binomial counts beat Poisson on the validation log score for these markets. Dispersion is fitted on 2022–24 and compared on 2024–25.
  • PRA dispersion is fitted directly against observed points + rebounds + assists. It preserves the aggregate's covariance and shared minutes variation rather than adding independent variances.
  • Available-player regulation minutes total 240 per team. Expected overtime is added separately. Current injuries exclude Out/Doubtful players; uncertain availability remains conditional on playing.
  • No historical injury reports, DNP model, confirmed starters or official minutes restrictions. New roles and rookies require caution.
  • No three-pointers-made model: made threes are absent from the player-level inputs. No historical prop prices, betting profitability claim or automatically generated bet recommendations.

Sources: NBA statistical definitions and SciPy count distribution documentation. Forecasts use the locally cached NBA game logs, schedule, rosters and injury feed.
